segs.p: Paṭhamajhānapañhāsutta
segs.e: A Question About the First Absorption

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Mahāmoggallāna was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There Venerable Mahāmoggallāna addressed the mendicants:

segs.p: “āvuso bhikkhave”ti.
segs.e: “Reverends, mendicants!”

segs.p: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend,” they replied.

segs.p: Āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca:
segs.e: Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this:

segs.p: “Idha mayhaṁ, āvuso, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi:
segs.e: “Just now, reverends, as I was in private retreat this thought came to mind:

segs.p: ‘paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ, paṭhamaṁ jhānan’ti vuccati.
segs.e: ‘They speak of this thing called the “first absorption”.

segs.p: Katamaṁ nu kho paṭhamaṁ jhānanti?
segs.e: What is the first absorption?’

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, āvuso, etadahosi:
segs.e: It occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘idha bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: ‘It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati paṭhamaṁ jhānan’ti.
segs.e: This is called the first absorption.’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And so … I was entering and remaining in the first absorption.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato kāmasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti.
segs.e: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by sensual pleasures beset me.

segs.p: Atha kho maṁ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

segs.p: ‘moggallāna, moggallāna.
segs.e: ‘Moggallāna, Moggallāna!

segs.p: Mā, brāhmaṇa, paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ pamādo, paṭhame jhāne cittaṁ saṇṭhapehi, paṭhame jhāne cittaṁ ekodiṁ karohi, paṭhame jhāne cittaṁ samādahā’ti.
segs.e: Don’t neglect the first absorption, brahmin! Settle your mind in the first absorption; unify your mind and immerse it in the first absorption.’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, aparena samayena vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja vihāsiṁ.
segs.e: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the first absorption.

segs.p: Yañhi taṁ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: So if anyone should be rightly called

segs.p: ‘satthārānuggahito sāvako mahābhiññataṁ patto’ti, mamaṁ taṁ sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

segs.p: ‘satthārānuggahito sāvako mahābhiññataṁ patto’”ti.
Paṭhamaṁ.

segs.p: Dutiyajhānapañhāsutta
segs.e: A Question About the Second Absorption

segs.e: “They speak of this thing called the ‘second absorption’.

segs.e: It occurred to me:

segs.e: ‘As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, a mendicant enters and remains in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati dutiyaṁ jhānan’ti.
segs.e: This is called the second absorption.’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā ajjhattaṁ sampasādanaṁ cetaso ekodibhāvaṁ avitakkaṁ avicāraṁ samādhijaṁ pītisukhaṁ dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.

segs.e: a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

segs.p: Tatiyajhānapañhāsutta
segs.e: A Question About the Third Absorption

segs.p: “‘Tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ, tatiyaṁ jhānan’ti vuccati.
segs.e: “They speak of this thing called the ‘third absorption’.

segs.p: Katamaṁ nu kho tatiyaṁ jhānanti?
segs.e: What is the third absorption?

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, āvuso, etadahosi—
segs.e: It occurred to me:

segs.p: idha bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṁvedeti, yaṁ taṁ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: ‘With the fading away of rapture, a mendicant enters and remains in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, “Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.”

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati tatiyaṁ jhānanti.
segs.e: This is called the third absorption.’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharāmi sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṁvedemi. Yaṁ taṁ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And so … I was entering and remaining in the third absorption.

segs.p: Catutthajhānapañhāsutta
segs.e: A Question About the Fourth Absorption

segs.p: “‘Catutthaṁ jhānaṁ, catutthaṁ jhānan’ti vuccati.

segs.e: ‘It’s when, with the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, a mendicant enters and remains in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

segs.p: Ākāsānañcāyatanapañhāsutta
segs.e: A Question About the Dimension of Infinite Space

segs.p: “‘Ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ, ākāsānañcāyatanan’ti vuccati.
segs.e: “They speak of this thing called the ‘dimension of infinite space’.

segs.e: It occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘idha bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ananto ākāsoti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: ‘It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that “space is infinite”, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati ākāsānañcāyatanan’ti.
segs.e: This is called the dimension of infinite space.’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ananto ākāsoti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And so … I was entering and remaining in the dimension of infinite space.

segs.p: Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanapañhāsutta
segs.e: A Question About the Dimension of Neither Perception Nor Non-Perception

segs.p: “‘Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanan’ti vuccati.
segs.e: “They speak of this thing called the ‘dimension of neither perception nor non-perception’.

segs.p: Katamaṁ nu kho nevasaññānāsaññāyatananti?
segs.e: What is the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception?

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, āvuso, etadahosi:
segs.e: It occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘idha bhikkhu sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: ‘It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, enters and remains in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: Idaṁ vuccati nevasaññānāsaññāyatanan’ti.
segs.e: This is called the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And so … I was entering and remaining in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato ākiñcaññāyatanasahagatā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti.
segs.e: While I was in that meditation, perception and focus accompanied by the dimension of nothingness beset me.

segs.p: Atha kho maṁ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

segs.p: ‘moggallāna, moggallāna.
segs.e: ‘Moggallāna, Moggallāna!

segs.p: Mā, brāhmaṇa, nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ pamādo, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ saṇṭhapehi, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ ekodiṁ karohi, nevasaññānāsaññāyatane cittaṁ samādahā’ti.
segs.e: Don’t neglect the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, brahmin! Settle your mind in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception; unify your mind and immerse it in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, aparena samayena sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja vihāsiṁ.
segs.e: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: Yañhi taṁ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya …pe… mahābhiññataṁ patto”ti.
segs.e: So if anyone should be rightly called a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

segs.p: Animittapañhāsutta
segs.e: A Question About the Signless

segs.p: “‘Animitto cetosamādhi, animitto cetosamādhī’ti vuccati.
segs.e: “They speak of this thing called the ‘signless immersion of the heart’.

segs.p: Katamo nu kho animitto cetosamādhīti?
segs.e: What is the signless immersion of the heart?

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, āvuso, etadahosi:
segs.e: It occurred to me:

segs.p: ‘idha bhikkhu sabbanimittānaṁ amanasikārā animittaṁ cetosamādhiṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: ‘It’s when a mendicant, not focusing on any signs, enters and remains in the signless immersion of the heart.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati animitto cetosamādhī’ti.
segs.e: This is called the signless immersion of the heart.’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, sabbanimittānaṁ amanasikārā animittaṁ cetosamādhiṁ upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And so … I was entering and remaining in the signless immersion of the heart.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, āvuso, iminā vihārena viharato nimittānusāri viññāṇaṁ hoti.
segs.e: While I was in that meditation, my consciousness followed after signs.

segs.p: Atha kho maṁ, āvuso, bhagavā iddhiyā upasaṅkamitvā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Buddha came up to me with his psychic power and said,

segs.p: ‘moggallāna, moggallāna.
segs.e: ‘Moggallāna, Moggallāna!

segs.p: Mā, brāhmaṇa, animittaṁ cetosamādhiṁ pamādo, animitte cetosamādhismiṁ cittaṁ saṇṭhapehi, animitte cetosamādhismiṁ cittaṁ ekodiṁ karohi, animitte cetosamādhismiṁ cittaṁ samādahā’ti.
segs.e: Don’t neglect the signless immersion of the heart, brahmin! Settle your mind in the signless immersion of the heart; unify your mind and immerse it in the signless immersion of the heart.’

segs.p: So khvāhaṁ, āvuso, aparena samayena sabbanimittānaṁ amanasikārā animittaṁ cetosamādhiṁ upasampajja vihāsiṁ.
segs.e: And so, after some time … I entered and remained in the signless immersion of the heart.

segs.p: Yañhi taṁ, āvuso, sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: So if anyone should be rightly called

segs.p: ‘satthārānuggahito sāvako mahābhiññataṁ patto’ti, mamaṁ taṁ sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: a disciple who attained to great direct knowledge with help from the Teacher, it’s me.”

segs.p: ‘satthārānuggahito sāvako mahābhiññataṁ patto’”ti.

segs.p: Sakkasutta
segs.e: With Sakka

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—jetavane antarahito devesu tāvatiṁsesu pāturahosi.
segs.e: And then Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared among the gods of the thirty-three.

segs.p: Atha kho sakko devānamindo pañcahi devatāsatehi saddhiṁ yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitaṁ kho sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Sakka, lord of gods, with five hundred deities came up to Mahāmoggallāna, bowed, and stood to one side. Mahāmoggallāna said to him:

segs.p: “Sādhu kho, devānaminda, buddhasaraṇagamanaṁ hoti.
segs.e: “Lord of gods, it’s good to go for refuge to the Buddha.

segs.p: Buddhasaraṇagamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti.
segs.e: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Sādhu kho, devānaminda, dhammasaraṇagamanaṁ hoti.

segs.e: It’s good to go for refuge to the Saṅgha.

segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti.
segs.e: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

segs.p: Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, devānaminda, evam’idhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti.
segs.e: It’s the reason why some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.e: It’s good to have experiential confidence in the Saṅgha:

segs.p: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṁ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons.
